subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should OpenClaw add a proactive normal-maintenance sweep for stale session archive artifacts beyond the existing deleted/reset retention helper, temp cleanup, and disk-budget paths?
rationale: The code paths show a real cleanup gap, but broad background deletion crosses session artifact retention policy and should not be chosen automatically while a narrower open PR already covers deleted/reset reporting.

options.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
options.body: Define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts should be removed automatically, under which mode and retention settings.

options.title: Land Narrow Reporting First
options.body: Treat the open PR as the immediate fix for deleted/reset cleanup visibility and leave proactive `.bak.*` and timer cleanup for later evidence.

options.title: Split By Artifact Class
options.body: Keep this issue as a parent and move each artifact class into a narrower canonical issue with its own proof and retention rule.

recommendation.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Define which `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.tmp`, `.bak.*`, checkpoint, and trajectory artifacts should be removed automatically, under which mode and retention settings.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the cleanup command and maintenance policy surface that this decision would extend.
